The underlying PISA design is a complex, stratified multistage sample of schools and students, and OECD typically provides sampling weights (and replicate weights) in the database to support population-representative estimates and correct uncertainty quantification. Because this factsheet does not specify which weight variables (e.g., student sampling weights or replicate weights) were applied in the reported figures, the exact weighting variable names are not extractable from the provided text. The factsheet also does not describe any plausible-values (PV) or missing-data processing steps, but PISA achievement reporting is based on the OECD’s standard scaling and PV framework in the PISA database.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet for Saudi Arabia summarizes how 15-year-old students performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed since Saudi Arabia’s first participation in 2018. It reports mean performance comparisons to the OECD average, trends from 2018 to 2022, and the distribution of students across proficiency levels (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6) for each domain. The factsheet also highlights subgroup patterns, including socioeconomic divides (ESCS quintiles), gender differences, and immigrant background differences, alongside indicators of school climate and student well-being (belonging, safety, bullying) and learning during COVID-related closures. It notes that PISA 2022 was delayed by one year due to COVID-19 and that some countries may have sampling-standard issues (marked with an asterisk), while Saudi Arabia’s data met quality standards. No machine-learning modeling is conducted in this factsheet; it is a descriptive benchmark report based on the OECD PISA 2022 Database.
